clue.text: Our mag's sexy look

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Private Eye is called ... by its readers
second meaning: to give someone ... is to look at them suggestively

explanation.walkthrough: The magazine is referring to itself.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The Eye' is the short title of Private Eye, and giving someone the eye is a flirtatious gaze.

clue.text: Practice outlawed by Thatcher — or one of many victims of her economic policy?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a workplace where union membership is compulsory, banned by her governments

definitions.text: one of many victims of her economic policy
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a shop closed down in the recession

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase literally: a shop that has closed.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatcher's union laws ended compulsory union membership, and her recessions shut many high-street businesses.

clue.text: Tebbit-inspired self-motivator?

parts.note: Norman Tebbit said his father got on his bike to look for work, and a bike rider moves himself along

explanation.walkthrough: Tebbit's 1981 speech gave rise to the jeer 'on yer bike' at the unemployed; the rider powers himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider of a pedal bike is propelled by his own legs, literally self-motivated.

clue.text: If Warren Beatty gets on top of one, ring his employer!

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece on top comes first

parts.note: the actor was famed as a womaniser, a stud
I is the Roman numeral one
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A joke about Warren Beatty's love life and calling his boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets on top of' puts STUD above I in this down answer, then O, the ring, follows. The 'if' clause reads as gossip, but Beatty is just a stud.
explanation.definitionFit: A film studio employs actors like Beatty, so it is his employer.

clue.text: Unwise to get your teeth into such a job!

definitions.text: Unwise to get your teeth into such a job!

parts.words: Unwise to get your teeth into such a job!
parts.note: a crude joke: biting is the last thing wanted in this oral sex act

explanation.walkthrough: 'Get your teeth into' usually means tackle with enthusiasm; here it is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow job is slang for fellatio, where teeth are notoriously unwelcome.

clue.text: One bent on buggering up airline's flipping new route?

indicators.note: flipping turns the airline's name over, so it reads backwards

parts.note: BA is British Airways, with the S of the possessive

indicators.note: new means the letters are formed into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A rogue intent on wrecking an airline's plan for a new route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns BA'S into SAB, and 'new' rearranges ROUTE into OTEUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A saboteur deliberately wrecks things, so someone set on messing them up.

clue.text: Truss fitted in minor operation — the scourge of many a father!

definitions.text: the scourge of many a father

indicators.note: something fitted in is put inside, so the truss goes inside the minor operation

parts.note: a minor is a young person under age, and an operation is an organisation or bureau doing official work
a truss is a surgical support

explanation.surface: A hernia truss fitted during a small operation, with a joke about what really torments fathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fitted in' places the truss inside the minor operation. The agency was the UK body set up in 1993 to chase absent fathers for maintenance, and was hated by many of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The agency forced separated fathers to pay maintenance, and many saw it as a persecutor.

clue.text: Leader calls for return of Eye's salutatory column. Thanks! Yes! (as Di might say)

indicators.note: a return is a trip back, so the whole string of greetings is read from end to start

parts.note: Private Eye parodied Hello! magazine under the title Hallo!, a greeting
ta is informal British thanks
ya, or yah, is the posh Sloane way of saying yes, as Princess Di might

explanation.surface: A leader demanding the return of a magazine's greetings page, with Princess Diana's posh thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader calls for return' suggests a politician, but the leader is the answer and 'calls for return of' is the reversal signal. HALLO, TA and YA together run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayatollah is a senior Shia cleric, and Ayatollah Khomeini led Iran after his return from exile.

clue.text: Scene of Terry's seizure that's swimming in aftershave

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the aftershave

parts.note: Brut is a brand of aftershave

indicators.note: swimming suggests letters floating out of place

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A man called Terry having a fit while drenched in cologne.
explanation.walkthrough: Terry Waite, the Archbishop of Canterbury's envoy, was kidnapped in Beirut in 1987. 'swimming' turns IE into EI.
explanation.definitionFit: Waite was seized and held hostage in the Lebanese capital for almost five years.

clue.text: The latest projected Virgin direction on rock

parts.note: virgin means new, unused
S is the compass abbreviation for south
to rock is to reel, sway unsteadily

explanation.surface: Richard Branson's Virgin company heading off in a fresh direction into rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virgin' looks like Branson's company but is just an adjective meaning unused.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsreel was a short cinema film of current events, so the latest happenings shown on a screen.

clue.text: Where shit's shovelled regularly in the Eye?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: on a farm, where muck is shifted
second meaning: the name of a regular Private Eye column about agriculture

explanation.walkthrough: 'Down on the Farm' is a long-running Private Eye column on farming scandals, written under the name Old Muckspreader.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm is where muck is shovelled, and the phrase is also the title of a regular magazine column.

clue.text: It's Lord Gnome's opinion Brenda sort of shot first

indicators.note: first means the shot comes before Brenda in the answer

parts.note: lead shot is a kind of ammunition
Private Eye nicknames the Queen Brenda, and ER is her royal cipher

explanation.surface: The proprietor's view on the Queen shooting first, a royal hunting scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Gnome is Private Eye's fictional proprietor, and Brenda is the Eye's nickname for the Queen. 'first' puts the shot ahead of her.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader is a newspaper's editorial column, setting out the proprietor's or editor's view.

clue.text: What Brillo Pad did to acquire a lot of bucks — flagellated

indicators.note: acquiring something takes it in, so the bucks go inside the action

parts.note: a Brillo pad is a scouring pad, and Brillo was the Eye's nickname for editor Andrew Neil
G is slang for a grand, a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: Andrew Neil, nicknamed Brillo Pad, earning a fortune and being thrashed for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye called Sunday Times editor Andrew Neil Brillo for his wiry hair. 'to acquire' puts G, a grand, inside SCOURED.
explanation.definitionFit: To scourge is to whip, and flagellation is whipping, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Strict control about to be imposed on Fleet Street gets no one's backing

indicators.note: something imposed on another is placed in front of it here

parts.note: re means about, concerning
London's Fleet Street was the home of the national press

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so these letters are read the other way

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A warning about censorship of the newspapers that finds no supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be imposed on' sets the word for about in front of the press, and 'backing' turns no plus one round to make ION.
explanation.definitionFit: Repression is harsh control that keeps people or ideas down.

clue.text: Have sex holding leftie hero's chopper

indicators.note: one thing holding another has it inside

parts.note: to mate is to have sex
Che Guevara is a hero of the left

explanation.surface: A smutty line about sex and a revolutionary's 'chopper', slang for penis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' invites the slang reading, but it is simply a blade. 'holding' puts Guevara's name inside the word for having sex.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad cutting blade used for chopping vegetation.

clue.text: Her vice: getting screwed by a good performer

indicators.note: by means beside, so the letter stands next to the jumble
screwed means twisted, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A woman's vice is sleeping with a talented performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting screwed' twists HER VICE into CHIEVER, and 'by' sets A beside it; the surface means screwed crudely.
explanation.definitionFit: An achiever is someone who succeeds, so someone who performs well.

clue.text: See 7
Old city curse is rather bland

parts.note: Ur was an ancient Mesopotamian city
a bane is a curse, a source of ruin

explanation.surface: An ancient city's curse turns out disappointingly mild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bland' here is the older sense of smooth and suave in manner, not tasteless.
explanation.definitionFit: Urbane means suave and polished in manner, which is close to bland in its sense of smoothly agreeable.

clue.text: See 11
See 25
Camelot's top man, a bit of a wide boy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: King ... ruled at Camelot

definitions.text: a bit of a wide boy
definitions.meaning: second meaning: ... Daley, the shady dealer in the TV series Minder

explanation.walkthrough: A wide boy is British slang for a small-time crook; Arthur Daley was the classic example in the ITV series Minder.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary king held court at Camelot, and Minder's dodgy dealer shares his first name.

clue.text: Regulation crappy first half of Baywatch includes bit of the Beeb's flop

indicators.note: includes means the anagram goes around the next piece
crappy means badly made, so these letters are rearranged
first half of picks the opening four letters of Baywatch

parts.note: Eldorado was a notorious BBC soap flop; its first bit is EL

explanation.surface: A rule about trashy TV: bad early Baywatch with a slice of a BBC failure.
explanation.walkthrough: Eldorado, a 1992 BBC soap set in Spain, was axed after one year and is the Beeb's famous flop.
explanation.definitionFit: A byelaw is a local regulation made by a council or other body.

clue.text: See 7
Let's scupper Mitterrand internally

indicators.note: internally means the letters are found inside the run of words

parts.note: the end of scupper and the start of Mitterrand run together to spell the answer

explanation.surface: A call to sink the French President's plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'internally' says the answer sits inside 'scupper Mitterrand'. 'Let's' reads as 'let us', but it is the verb 'lets', allows.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit is to allow, so it lets someone do something.

clue.text: She took corrective action to avoid stroke

parts.note: to miss is to avoid
a whiplash is a stroke of a whip

explanation.surface: A woman taking remedial steps to avoid a stroke, a medical scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stroke' looks medical, but it is a lash. Miss Whiplash was the professional name of Lindi St Clair, a dominatrix who founded the Corrective Party.
explanation.definitionFit: She administered 'correction' as a dominatrix and stood for Parliament for the Corrective Party.

clue.text: Knackered professional

definitions.meaning: first meaning: worn out, done for
second meaning: ... as in polished, accomplished

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look almost opposite, one exhausted and one expert, yet one word covers both.
explanation.definitionFit: Finished means exhausted, and a finished performance is polished and accomplished.

clue.text: Bloody conservative close to the Kremlin

parts.note: red is the colour of blood
a square is a conventional, old-fashioned person

explanation.surface: A cruel hardliner in the Russian government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' is a noun here: an enclosed space next to the Kremlin.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Square is the great Moscow plaza that runs alongside the Kremlin walls.

clue.text: Charlie's runaway catches cold — the mutt!

indicators.note: catching something takes it inside, so cold goes into the runaway

parts.note: Pooh was Prince Charles's Jack Russell terrier, which went missing at Balmoral in 1994
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Prince Charles's lost dog catching a chill: the poor mutt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catches' puts C inside POOH. Charles's terrier Pooh vanished on a walk at Balmoral and was never found.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooch is informal for a dog, and mutt is another informal word for one.
